resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1933 Coos Bay Times reports the tower as 60 feet; the register and firelookout.com say a 40-foot pole L-4. The brief's 18.3 m (60 ft) follows the newspaper; the story reports both.

A July 1929 newspaper says the primary station near Bridge was completed that spring, and an April 1929 item said a lookout would be erected that summer. The 1933 papers describe a new 60-foot tower being built. Register and firelookout.com date the tower to 1933, which matches the newspapers. The sources do not say whether a tower stood in 1929, so the story does not date the tower before 1933.
Not contradictory: the newspaper records abandonment in July 1955, and the register and firelookout.com record removal or destruction in 1956.

notes_for_editor: The 60 ft vs 40 ft height conflict is unresolved; the story reports both. The Forest Lookouts page is a compilation of Coos Bay Times and Myrtle Point Herald clippings. Its April 1929 item says the Forest Service would erect a lookout that summer; its July 1929 item says the primary station was completed that spring. Neither says whether a tower stood in 1929, so the story no longer says the tower came later. One search returned no current description of the site; no photos captured (the register page shows collection photos from 1933-1956 but no image URLs were captured).
